steps.prompt_exact: Forking from the checklist version that has Essentials/Nice-to-have filters and a next-5 summary: turn this into a one-file family road-trip readiness board with lanes for each traveler, pets, car prep, and timing buckets. Keep it editable and make the next-action strip obvious.
steps.response_exact:
I will fork from the filtered checklist state and keep the useful next-action idea, but change the product direction from a generic weekend checklist into a family road-trip readiness board.

The fork will keep the same single-file browser-tool shape and add lanes for People, Pets, Car, Before leaving, On the road, and Arrival. Each item can be checked off, filtered by priority, and summarized in a next-action strip so someone can sit down and immediately know what to do first.
steps.notes: Simulated fork prompt. It branches from the original response package 03 before the source path continued into timing groups.

steps.prompt_exact: Make the board feel ready for someone to use before leaving: add default sample items, a clear print/export summary, and a compact mobile layout while keeping it one self-contained HTML file.
steps.response_exact:
Done.

I tightened the fork into a publishable one-file road-trip readiness board. It now opens with sample family-trip items, keeps a next-action strip at the top, supports priority and lane filters, lets the user add custom tasks, and includes a print-friendly summary for the trip handoff.
